title: Token refresh race condition causing org-scoped credential leakage across Dedicated & Private runtimes
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: Several customers on Dedicated and Private deployments reported erroneous authorization checks after token refresh events. When a long-lived session triggers a token refresh while concurrent requests for different org contexts are in-flight, the refreshed credential can be associated with the wrong org scope. This leads to transient access to another org's resources (read-only in observed cases) and multiple customer escalations.

Observed impact: 1) Rare but reproducible cross-org authorization checks returning success for the wrong org id for up to a few seconds. 2) Affected deployment modes: Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with shared control-plane routing) and Private (VPC with local control-plane mirrors). 3) Customers reporting: FinBank (production incident), MedQ Analytics (escalation to CSM), Retailly (support ticket).

Why this ticket exists: Full investigation, customer mitigation, patch, and rollout plan to prevent recurrence and obtain an emergency release for affected Dedicated/Private clusters.
steps_to_reproduce: Use a client with a session that retains a refresh token and make rapid concurrent requests (30-200ms inter-request) across two different org-scoped sessions (org A and org B).
Force token expiry on the auth service (shorten token TTL in staging) and trigger refresh from both session contexts simultaneously.
Observe request traces: some requests that originated with org A are authorized using the refreshed token metadata for org B (check authorization headers/logged org_id in control-plane audit logs).
Reproduction is flaky on small clusters; reliably reproducible with 10+ concurrent clients and artificially-short token TTLs in a staging Dedicated cluster.
root_cause: Race in the token refresh path: the auth refresh worker writes refreshed token metadata into a shared in-memory cache (control-plane cache) keyed only by token id, not by session+org context. Concurrent requests read cache entries while the refresh write is in progress; because writes are not atomic at the required granularity and the control-plane routing sometimes multiplexes sessions, the token->org mapping can be transiently incorrect. Additional contributing factors: different control-plane sync behavior between Hosted (correct) vs Dedicated/Private (eventual sync with local mirrors), and a regression introduced in runtime-2.4.0 where the refresh write was moved to an asynchronous goroutine to reduce latency without proper locking.
mitigations: Hotfix: Revert async write by forcing synchronous refresh write and compare metadata before swapping (PATCH in staging applied 2026-03-06).
Customer mitigation: Recommended short-term rollback of token TTL from customers to avoid frequent refresh churn and temporary configuration to reduce concurrent cross-org session sharing.
Access control: Added temporary deny-rule to limit cross-org proxying for at-risk clusters; enforced rate limiter on refresh endpoints to reduce concurrent refreshes.
proposed_fix: Primary fix: Introduce per-session (session_id + org_id) refresh cache key and an atomic compare-and-swap for refresh writes. Also add a conservative lock per token id with 50ms backoff to serialize refresh logic in control-plane. A more durable fix will include schema change to persist org_id in the token metadata store and make refresh idempotent. Implementation PR will include unit tests that simulate interleaved refresh + request patterns and an e2e test in a dedicated staging cluster.
rollout_plan: 1) Patch code and run full test-suite + chaos e2e in staging (target: 2026-03-10).
2) Smoke deploy to 1 Dedicated customer cluster with AVAILABILITY_MODE=canary (2026-03-11).
3) Monitor auth-audit logs and run script to validate no cross-org hits for 24h; if clean, roll to remaining Dedicated clusters (2026-03-12 to 2026-03-13).
4) For Private customers we will provide the patch as a private upgrade bundle and coordinate with SRE/CS for handoff (target: 2026-03-14 to 2026-03-18).
5) Publish postmortem and security advisory once rollout complete.

MedQ Analytics - Sev 2 - requested immediate remediation 2026-03-06
